entry.title: Praia de Porto Pim, Horta
entry.summary: Porto Pim is a sheltered curved bay on Faial next to Horta, with grey-gold sand, calm water and a view of Monte da Guia. It is good for swimming and snorkelling, and the old whaling museum is nearby. The Horta marina is a short walk away.

entry.title: Praia Formosa, Santa Maria
entry.summary: Praia Formosa is the main sandy beach on Santa Maria, the only Azores island with real golden sand. It is a wide beach with clear water, backed by a lawn and bar, and hosts a well-known music festival in August. The water stays cooler than the mainland.

entry.title: Praia do Vau, Portimao
entry.summary: Praia do Vau is a sandy cove near Portimao in the Algarve, enclosed by golden cliffs and rock stacks. The water is clear and the beach has lifeguards and restaurants behind it. A cliff path leads to neighbouring beaches.

entry.title: Praia da Oura, Albufeira
entry.summary: Praia da Oura is a wide golden beach backed by low cliffs just east of the Albufeira old town. It has beach bars, lifeguards and calm water, and the lively Strip is close. It is busy in July and August but easy to reach.

entry.title: Grama Bay, Karaburun
entry.summary: Grama Bay is a sheltered cove on the Karaburun peninsula, with a pebble beach, clear water and inscriptions carved into the rock by ancient visitors. It is mostly visited by boat from Vlore. There are no facilities on shore.

entry.title: Porto Palermo Beach, Himara
entry.summary: Porto Palermo is a sheltered bay on the Albanian Riviera near Himara, with a pebble beach and a small Ali Pasha castle on the peninsula. The water is clear and calm. A few cafes sit near the bay and the setting is quiet.

entry.title: Shengjin Beach, Lezhe
entry.summary: Shengjin is a small port town on the Adriatic coast of northern Albania with a long sandy beach, a promenade and many cafes and hotels. The water is shallow and warm, which suits families. It is far less crowded than the better-known resorts further south.

entry.title: Anchor Bay, Popeye Village
entry.summary: Anchor Bay is a small pebble and rock bay below Popeye Village on the north-west coast of Malta, framed by cliffs and the colourful film-set village. The water is clear and sheltered. Entry to the village is ticketed and the beach is small.

entry.title: Fond Ghadir, Sliema
entry.summary: Fond Ghadir is a rocky swim spot on the Sliema seafront in Malta, with flat platforms, ladders and clear water beside the promenade. There is no sand. It is very convenient for a quick swim from the city, and there is a lido nearby.

entry.title: Marsalforn Bay, Gozo
entry.summary: Marsalforn is a small town on the north coast of Gozo with a sheltered bay, a small beach of sand and pebbles and a promenade lined with restaurants and cafes. The water is clear and calm in summer. Dive centres operate here and the rocks nearby are good for snorkelling.

entry.title: Qbajjar Bay, Gozo
entry.summary: Qbajjar Bay is a rocky bay on the north coast of Gozo near Marsalforn, next to the old salt pans. Swimming is from the flat rocks into clear water and there are a few restaurants nearby. It is a quiet spot, but there is little sand.

entry.title: Wied il-Ghasri, Gozo
entry.summary: Wied il-Ghasri is a narrow inlet cut into the cliffs on the north-west coast of Gozo, reached by steps down the gorge. A small area of sand and pebbles sits at the bottom and the water is very clear. There are no facilities and the sea can be rough, so it suits calm days.

entry.title: Ghar Lapsi, Siggiewi
entry.summary: Ghar Lapsi is a small rocky inlet on the south-west coast of Malta near Siggiewi, with ladders and flat rock platforms for swimming and no sand. The water is deep and very clear, which makes it a popular spot with divers and snorkellers. A couple of restaurants overlook the inlet.

entry.title: Veliki Pijesak Beach, Ulcinj
entry.summary: Veliki Pijesak is a sandy beach near Ulcinj on the south Montenegrin coast, with shallow warm water that suits families. Beach bars and cafes line the shore in summer. The wider Ulcinj area is known for its long sandy beaches and warm sea.

entry.title: Plavi Horizonti Beach, Lustica
entry.summary: Plavi Horizonti is a wide, clean beach on the Lustica peninsula, with fine pebbles, some sand and very clear water. The sea gets deep gradually. Beach bars and restaurants are set behind the shore and there is parking nearby.

entry.title: Zanjice Beach, Lustica
entry.summary: Zanjice is a pebble bay on the Lustica peninsula at the mouth of the Bay of Kotor, with a view of Mamula island. The water is clear and boat trips run to the nearby Blue Cave. A restaurant and beach bar sit behind the shore, and the road down is narrow.

entry.title: Novi Vinodolski Beach, Kvarner
entry.summary: Novi Vinodolski sits on the Kvarner coast, with a long pebble beach running along a palm-lined promenade and a small fortress above the harbour. The sea is clean and gets deep quite fast. It is a relaxed resort town with plenty of cafes behind the beach.

entry.title: Petrcane Beach, Zadar
entry.summary: Petrcane is a former fishing village about 10 km north of Zadar, with a pebble beach beside a promenade and a small harbour. The water is shallow and clear, so it is a good option for children. The village has restaurants and a calmer feel than central Zadar.

entry.title: Borik Beach, Zadar
entry.summary: Borik is the main city beach of Zadar, a stretch of pebbles and concrete platforms with a promenade, hotels and cafes behind it. The sea is clear and gets deep gradually. It is easy to reach by bus or on foot from the old town area, and has everything a day visit needs.

entry.title: Lovrecina Bay, Brac
entry.summary: Lovrecina is a sheltered bay near Postira on the north coast of Brac, with fine pebbles and sand, shallow clear water and pine trees behind the beach. A short stone building at one end is a former chapel. It is popular with families and quieter than Zlatni Rat.

entry.title: Prapratno Beach, Peljesac
entry.summary: Prapratno is a long sheltered bay on the Peljesac peninsula, a few kilometres from Ston, with a mix of fine pebbles and sand and pine trees right behind the shore. The water is shallow and calm, so it suits families. The ferry to Mljet leaves from the nearby port.

entry.title: Platja de Sant Pol, Costa Brava
entry.summary: Platja de Sant Pol is a wide crescent of golden sand on the Costa Brava just north of Sant Feliu de Guixols, backed by a promenade and pine-covered hills. The water is clear and shallow, and a coastal path leads to the neighbouring cove of s Agaro. Restaurants and cafes line the seafront.

entry.title: Agios Georgios Beach, Naxos
entry.summary: Agios Georgios is the town beach of Naxos, a long strip of sand with shallow, calm water just a short walk south of the old harbour. Tavernas and rooms stand behind the beach, and the shallow water makes it a good choice for families. The beach is sheltered, though the summer wind can be strong.

entry.title: Baia Sardinia Beach
entry.summary: Baia Sardinia is a small resort on the Costa Smeralda in north-east Sardinia, with a sheltered bay of coarse sand, granite rocks and clear water. Pine trees and Mediterranean scrub rise behind the shore, and the harbour stands at one end of the bay. Boats leave for the islands of the La Maddalena archipelago.

entry.title: Mastichari Beach, Kos
entry.summary: Mastichari is a small fishing village on the north-west coast of Kos, with a long beach of sand and fine pebbles, shallow water and a gentle slope into the sea. The wind is often steady here, so the beach is popular with kitesurfers, and boats leave from the harbour for the island of Kalymnos.

entry.title: Praia da Fuseta, Algarve
entry.summary: Praia da Fuseta is a long, quiet beach of fine sand on a barrier island in the Ria Formosa lagoon of the eastern Algarve, reached by a short ferry or footbridge from the fishing village of Fuseta. The beach is wide and calm, with few buildings and shallow water on the lagoon side.

entry.title: Praia de Matosinhos, Porto
entry.summary: Praia de Matosinhos is a wide urban beach of golden sand just north of the port of Porto, with Atlantic waves and a long promenade. The seafront has a large collection of fish restaurants, and surfers and walkers use the beach all year. The water is cool and the waves can be strong.

entry.title: Agia Galini Beach, Crete
entry.summary: Agia Galini is a fishing village on the south coast of Crete, built on a hillside above a small harbour, with a beach of dark sand and pebbles beside the village. Warm water and a lively harbour with tavernas make it a popular base for trips to the beaches of Agios Pavlos and Preveli.

entry.title: Agia Pelagia Beach, Crete
entry.summary: Agia Pelagia is a small resort on the north coast of Crete west of Heraklion, with a curved bay of sand and coarse pebbles and a calm sea. Green hills rise on both sides of the bay, and a few tavernas stand along the water. The nearby beaches of Lygaria and Fodele can be reached by car.

entry.title: Almyrida Beach, Crete
entry.summary: Almyrida is a small village on the north coast of Crete east of Chania, with a long sandy beach, shallow calm water and a gentle slope into the sea. The beach is protected by a small headland and is popular with families. A few tavernas and rooms stand along the shore.
